title: Divine LLaMAs: Bias, Stereotypes, Stigmatization, and Emotion Representation of Religion in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: Analysis of bias, stereotypes, and stigmatization in how Large Language Models attribute emotions to different religious personas.
base_benchmarks: ISEAR (International Survey on Emotion Antecedents and Reactions) dataset
findings: LLMs represent major Western religions (Christianity) with more nuance, while Eastern religions (Hinduism, Buddhism) are heavily stereotyped. Judaism and Islam are stigmatized, leading to significantly higher response refusal rates, particularly from Llama family models. Models like Mistral and GPT-4o exhibit less exaggerated safety. Models tend to over-attribute 'compassion' to Buddhists and are inconsistent in generating sacred or religion-specific emotions, sometimes confusing them with religious principles like 'dharma'.
references: Abubakar Abid, Maheen Farooqi, and James Zou. 2021. Persistent anti-muslim bias in large language models. In Proceedings of the 2021 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society, pages 298–306.
